newsitem.title: CHINA: Musical nearly left waiting by baggage carousel.
newsitem.headline: Musical nearly left waiting by baggage carousel.

text.p: Luggage going astray is the nightmare of every air traveller, especially if the luggage in question is a HK$15.6 million (US$2 million) stage set just before opening night.

Less than 12 hours before the curtain was to go up in Hong Kong on a travelling production of "The Sound of Music" starring U.S. singer Marie Osmond, a bird flew into the engine of the jet chartered to fly the set from Bangkok, the South China Morning Post reported on Saturday.
Then, when the plane finally arrived at 10 a.m. on the day of the opening, the aircraft was impounded by drug investigators as part of a search of all flights from Thailand.
By the time the set got to the theatre with seven hours to go, it had been soaked in the torrential rains tormenting the territory recently and had to be repainted.
With 110 extra stage hands brought in by producers, the curtain went up on Wednesday just 35 minutes late -- but with some banging of hammers behind the sound of music, the paper said.
